title: Hanno the Navigator down the African coast, c. 500 BC
summary: Sixty fifty-oared ships and thirty thousand settlers leave Carthage for the Atlantic coast of Africa, found cities beyond the Pillars of Heracles, and sail on past the river Lixos to a fiery mountain and an island of hairy people, the Gorillai.

legs.source: the Periplus does not give the Mediterranean leg; the way along the African shore
the Periplus: Thymiaterion, Soloeis, five cities, Lixos, then Cerne
legs.note: Cerne is identified with Herne Island at Rio de Oro, one place among several proposed

legs.source: the Periplus; the Chretes river is usually read as the Senegal
the Periplus tells of fire and the Horn of the West; the Mount of the Chariot of the Gods is variously Mount Cameroon or the Guinean highlands
the Periplus: the Horn of the South, the island of the hairy people; the fiery mountain is conventionally Mount Cameroon
legs.note: the furthest the text goes, short of food

events.label: Cerne, Hanno’s base on the Atlantic coast
events.text: The Periplus says Hanno of Carthage sailed with sixty ships of fifty oars and 30,000 settlers to found colonies on the coast of Libya, as Africa was then called. Cerne was the island where they settled. Where it was, from Morocco to Senegal, is still debated.

events.label: The Chariot of the Gods and the Gorillai
events.text: Fire in the sea, streams of it running down a mountain, and the "Chariot of the Gods":  a volcano, perhaps Mount Cameroon. Beyond it, a bay of hairy creatures the interpreters called Gorillai; the Carthaginians caught three females, who fought until they were killed, and took their skins home. Whether these were apes or people has been argued ever since; the gorilla took its name from them in 1847.
